questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

##### CELL 262 [markdown]
**Final model (run 2026-11-27, cross-validated inside 2000–15; test set untouched): logistic regression without source group.**
- AUC **0.769** (95% range 0.756–0.784) vs 0.767 with source group, and the baseline's 0.609. Top 20% picks: **precision 64%, recall 38.9%** (baseline 46% / 28.0%; best possible recall 60%). Top 10%: precision 71%.
- 37 terms; McFadden pseudo-R² 0.192; AIC 3,880 (vs 3,885 with source group: simpler and better).
- **All 12 remaining features pass the likelihood-ratio test** (p ≤ 0.008) and raise AIC when removed: budget, distributor group, MPAA rating, company track record, sequel, primary genre, origin, runtime, rating-overlap competition, director track record, release weekday, major producer.
- XGBoost challenger: AUC 0.758, precision 61%, recall 37.1%.
- Next: the single evaluation on 2016–19 (bootstrap CI vs baseline), then the 2020–23 stress test, after Matt signs off on A9.
##### CELL 263 [markdown]
## 21. Evaluation on the 2016–2019 test set (run once, 2026-11-27)

**This is the single, pre-committed test.** Everything is frozen before it runs:
- **Model:** logistic regression with the §20 final feature set (12 features, blank categories merged, no `_missing` flags), trained on **all** 2000–2015 films. Challenger: XGBoost, same features.
- **Baseline (b):** genre × budget-tier winner rate from 2000–2015 (smoothed, as in §18).
- **Selection:** the contract picks 20% **each year**, so the main result picks the top 20% within each release year (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019). The pooled top 20% of all test films is shown as a check.
- **Measures (A9):** share of all test winners in the picks (recall), share of picks that are winners (precision), and AUC.
- **Evidence bar:** beat the baseline by **≥ 5 points**, with a **bootstrap 95% CI** for the difference that excludes 0 (2,000 resamples of test films).
- Nothing below changes the model. Any change after this point would be tuned on the test set and must be reported that way.

yt = TEST["winner"].astype(int).values
print(f"Test films: {len(TEST):,} (2016-19); winners {yt.mean():.1%}; by year: {TEST.groupby('year').size().to_dict()}")


def prep(df, ref):
    """Same transformations as the training data (§19-20), with every choice learned from the training set `ref`."""
    d = df.copy()
    d["mpaa_rating"] = d["mpaa_rating"].replace({"NC-17": "R"})
    keep_genres = ref["primary_genre"].value_counts()
    keep_genres = set(keep_genres[keep_genres >= 40].index)
    d["primary_genre"] = d["primary_genre"].where(d["primary_genre"].isin(keep_genres), "Other")
    for c in ["director", "writer", "company"]:
        d[f"{c}_has_history"] = d[f"{c}_prior_hit_rate"].notna().astype(int)
    for c in CATS3:
        d[c] = d[c].astype(object).fillna("(blank)").astype(str)
        mode = X3.loc[X3[c] != "(blank)", c].mode()[0]          # training mode
        d[c] = d[c].replace("(blank)", mode)
    d["distributor_group"] = d["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
    return d[["log_budget"] + NUMS2 + CATS3]


Xtest = prep(TEST, TRN)

def pick_mask(score, idx_years, k=0.2, per_year=True, lowest=False):
    s = -score if lowest else score

    groups = [np.where(idx_years == y)[0] for y in np.unique(idx_years)] if per_year else [np.arange(len(s))]

I rebuilt the data on your machine and reran Tanner's notebook. **The final model reproduces his numbers exactly.** Two baseline-and-challenger figures moved by a hair, for harmless reasons explained below. All 270 cells ran with no errors.

**Final logistic regression (the model we're using):**

| Measure | Tanner (11/27) | My rerun |
|---|---|---|
| Test films 2016–19, winner rate | 855, 35.6% | 855, 35.6% |
| Cross-validation AUC (2000–15) | 0.769 | 0.769 |
| Test AUC | 0.831 | 0.831 |
| Test winners caught | 45.1% | 45.1% |
| Test picks that won | 80.1% | 80.1% |
| Calibration and per-year results | as reported | identical |

**Small differences:**
- **Baseline winners caught:** 31.6% vs Tanner's 31.9%. That's one film out of the 304 test winners. Many films share the same baseline score, and which one makes the cutoff depends on how the computer breaks ties. As a result, the gain over the baseline reads **+13.5 points** (95% CI +7.9 to +17.6) instead of +13.2. Either way it easily clears the 5-point bar.
- **XGBoost challenger:** AUC 0.828 vs 0.822. This is most likely a different XGBoost version on your machine, which gives slightly different randomness. It's still a tie with logistic regression, so the conclusion doesn't change.

**Two setup notes for the README:**
- **Tanner's notebooks ask for a kernel called `emba560-a10`,** which exists only on his machine. I ran them on your standard `python3` kernel instead.
- **Windows briefly blocked one scikit-learn file** on the first run. It cleared on its own and hasn't come back.

**This rerun doesn't count as Appendix D.** It reruns Tanner's code; it doesn't rebuild the numbers independently. It does confirm that the data and the code agree on your machine.

## 1. Business Understanding

From the Purpose Contract (`A10_purpose_contract_FROZEN_2026-11-17.md`) with amendments A1–A7, agreed by Tanner and Matt on 2026-11-24.

| Field | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Decision** (A6, A9) | Before a film's release, pick the films most likely to be **winners**; the rest get a closer look at their release and marketing plans before more money goes in. The screen never cancels or rejects a film on its own. |
| **Action** (A9) | Each year, the 20% of films most likely to be winners are identified. |
| **Inputs allowed** (A4, A6) | Anything the studio **controls before release**: budget, genre, runtime, release date, MPAA rating, director/writer/company track records (earlier films only), distributor, country, language, franchise, source material. Nothing known only after release (box office, reviews, scores, votes). |
| **Population** (A1, A2, A7) | Feature films **released in the US**, 2000–2023, budget ≥ $1M, after the cleaning rules in §3. Sensitivity rerun at a $100K floor. |
| **Label** (A3, A7, A9) | **Winner = US box office ≥ 1.25 × budget.** 1.25× US ≈ the industry rule of thumb of 2.5× worldwide (the US is about half of worldwide box office). It's a convention, not a data finding; rerun at 1× and 1.5×. |
| **Splits** (A5) | Train 2000–2015, test 2016–2019, stress test 2020–2023 (COVID era) reported separately. |
| **Baseline and bar** (A9) | Beat a genre × budget-tier rule by ≥ 5 percentage points in **winners caught in the top 20%**, with a bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0. |

**Framing (A9, agreed 2026-11-27):** the screen picks the 20% of films most likely to be **winners** (US box office ≥ 1.25× budget) each year.

##### E248 [markdown]
### 19b. Statistical fit of each feature (logistic regression, all 3,708 training films)

- **Pseudo-R² (McFadden):** 1 − (log-likelihood of the model ÷ log-likelihood of a model with no features). For logistic regression, 0.2–0.4 is considered a good fit.
- **AIC:** fit penalized for the number of parameters; lower is better. A feature earns its place if removing it **raises** AIC by more than about 2.
- **Likelihood-ratio test:** refit without the feature (all its categories at once) and test whether the fit got significantly worse (χ², p < 0.05 = keep).
- **Coefficient p-values:** for each single term (each category vs its reference, each standardized number). Budget uses log budget and its square, so its curve shows in two terms.

- **Sequel** 1.34×, **company hit rate** 1.32×, **Wednesday release** 1.48×, **more overlapping competition** 0.78×.
- **Budget is negative once everything else is known (0.43× per SD):** among films with the same distributor, rating and genre, cheaper films more often earn 1.25× back. Big budgets look good on their own only because they come with majors and sequels.

"""Replace A10-master §4-6 placeholder cell with standalone modeling and evaluation code promoted from Edwards-A10 §18-21."""
import json
import sys
import uuid

path = sys.argv[1]
nb = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))
cells = nb["cells"]
assert cells[31]["source"][0].startswith("## 4. Modeling"), "unexpected master layout"


def md(s):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "metadata": {}, "source": s.strip("\n").splitlines(True)}


def code(s):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "metadata": {}, "execution_count": None, "outputs": [],
            "source": s.strip("\n").splitlines(True)}


NEW = [
md(r'''
## 4. Modeling

Promoted from `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §18–20 (Tanner, 2026-11-26 to 11-27), rewritten to run on its own from `films_clean.csv`. Same features, settings, folds and seeds; nothing retuned.

**Framing (A9):** a **winner** = US box office ≥ 1.25× budget (`winner`). The model ranks films by their chance of being a winner; the screen picks the **top 20%**.

**Everything in §4 is 5-fold cross-validation inside the training years (2000–2015).** The 2016–19 test set is used once, in §5.

**Measures**
- **Recall @20%** (winners caught) = share of all winners that land in the top 20% picks. With 33% winners, random picks catch 20%; the best possible is 60%.
- **Precision @20%** (hit rate) = share of the picks that are winners (random: 33%).
- **AUC** = ranking quality over all films (0.5 = random, 1 = perfect).

**Ties:** picks use a stable sort (`kind="stable"`), so films with equal scores are always broken in the same order on every machine. Tanner's original used NumPy's default sort, which can break ties differently across machines. Only the baseline (many films share its group scores) can move, by about one film; model scores have no ties. Changed by Matt, 2026-11-28, before rerunning; not tuning.

### 4a. Setup
'''),
code(r'''
import warnings
from scipy.stats import chi2
import statsmodels.api as sm
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, log_loss
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler, SplineTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from xgboost import XGBClassifier

TRN = films[films["in_population"] & films["year"].le(2015)].reset_index(drop=True)
yl = TRN["winner"].astype(int).values
folds = list(StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=560).split(TRN, yl))
TIERS = ([0, 5e6, 20e6, 60e6, np.inf], ["$1-5M", "$5-20M", "$20-60M", "$60M+"])
print(f"Training films (2000-15): {len(TRN):,}; winners {yl.mean():.1%}; random picks catch 20% of winners, "
      f"best possible {min(1, 0.2 / yl.mean()):.0%}")


def top_k(score, k=0.2):
    """Indices of the top k share of films by score; stable sort so ties break the same way everywhere."""
    return np.argsort(-score, kind="stable")[:int(round(k * len(score)))]


def capture_at(score, y, k=0.2):
    top = top_k(score, k)
    return y[top].sum() / y.sum(), y[top].mean()


def cv_predict(model, X):
    oof = np.zeros(len(X))
    for tr_i, te_i in folds:
        model.fit(X.iloc[tr_i], yl[tr_i])
        oof[te_i] = model.predict_proba(X.iloc[te_i])[:, 1]
    return oof


def auc_range(s, y=yl, n=300, seed=560):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = [roc_auc_score(y[i], s[i]) for i in (rng.integers(0, len(y), len(y)) for _ in range(n))]
    return f"{np.percentile(b, 2.5):.3f}-{np.percentile(b, 97.5):.3f}"


def summary_row(name, s, with_logloss=True):
    cap, prec = capture_at(s, yl)
    return {"model": name, "AUC": round(roc_auc_score(yl, s), 3), "AUC 95% range": auc_range(s),
            "recall @20%": f"{cap:.1%}", "precision @20%": f"{prec:.1%}",
            "log loss": round(log_loss(yl, np.clip(s, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)), 3) if with_logloss else np.nan}
'''),
md(r'''
### 4b. Baseline (b): genre × budget tier

The bar to beat (contract, A9): each film gets the historical winner rate of its genre × budget-tier group, learned on the training folds only. Thin groups are pulled toward the average (20 pseudo-films).
'''),
code(r'''
g_b = TRN["primary_genre"].fillna("(blank)") + " | " + pd.cut(TRN["fin_budget"], *TIERS).astype(str)
oof_b = np.zeros(len(TRN))
for tr_i, te_i in folds:
    rates = pd.Series(yl[tr_i]).groupby(g_b.iloc[tr_i].values).agg(["sum", "size"])
    smooth = (rates["sum"] + 20 * yl[tr_i].mean()) / (rates["size"] + 20)
    oof_b[te_i] = g_b.iloc[te_i].map(smooth).fillna(yl[tr_i].mean()).values
rng = np.random.default_rng(560)
display(pd.DataFrame([summary_row("random 20%", rng.random(len(TRN)), False),
                      summary_row("baseline (b): genre x budget tier", oof_b, False)]).set_index("model").drop(columns="log loss"))
'''),
md(r'''
### 4c. Five model types on the same features

All inputs known before release (A6), **no `_missing` flags** (they leak the outcome: undocumented films are mostly flops; with them, AUC rises by about 0.04 for the wrong reason, `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §18). Same folds for every model.

| Model | In plain words |
|---|---|
| Logistic regression | one weight per feature; budget gets a curve (spline) |
| Decision tree | a single shallow tree, readable as if/then rules (depth 4) |
| Random forest | 500 trees averaged |
| Gradient boosting (scikit-learn) | trees built one after another, each fixing the last one's errors |
| XGBoost | the industry-standard version of gradient boosting |
'''),
code(r'''
D = TRN.copy()
D["mpaa_rating"] = D["mpaa_rating"].replace({"NC-17": "R"})                       # 9 NC-17 films merged into R
D["primary_genre"] = D["primary_genre"].where(D["primary_genre"].map(D["primary_genre"].value_counts()) >= 40, "Other")
D["original_language"] = D["original_language"].where(D["original_language"].isin(D["original_language"].value_counts().head(5).index), "other")
for c in ["director", "writer", "company"]:
    D[f"{c}_has_history"] = D[f"{c}_prior_hit_rate"].notna().astype(int)          # 'no earlier film' is its own signal
CATS = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday", "source_group", "original_language"]
NUMS = ["runtime_min", "release_month", "sequel", "major_producer", "director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history",
        "writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history", "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history",
        "rating_overlap_competition"]
for c in CATS:
    D[c] = D[c].astype(object).fillna("(blank)").astype(str)
Xall = D[["log_budget"] + NUMS + CATS]

pre_linear = ColumnTransformer([
    ("budget", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3)), ["log_budget"]),
    ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMS),
    ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20), CATS)])
pre_tree = ColumnTransformer([("num", "passthrough", ["log_budget"] + NUMS),
                              ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20, sparse_output=False), CATS)])


def xgb():
    return XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
                         min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=1.0, eval_metric="logloss", random_state=560, n_jobs=4)


MODELS = {
    "Logistic regression": make_pipeline(pre_linear, LogisticRegression(max_iter=3000, C=0.5)),
    "Decision tree": make_pipeline(pre_tree, SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=4, min_samples_leaf=50, random_state=560)),
    "Random forest": make_pipeline(pre_tree, SimpleImputer(strategy="median"),
                                   RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=500, min_samples_leaf=20, max_features="sqrt", n_jobs=-1, random_state=560)),
    "XGBoost": make_pipeline(pre_tree, xgb()),
}
OOF = {name: cv_predict(m, Xall) for name, m in MODELS.items()}

# Gradient boosting (scikit-learn) uses native categories (Edwards §18 "cleanest" version: no _missing flags, distributor Blank = unknown)
Xhgb = TRN[["log_budget"] + [c for c in NUMS if not c.endswith("_has_history")]].astype(float).copy()
for c in CATS:
    s = TRN[c].astype(object)
    if c == "distributor_group":
        s = s.where(s.ne("Blank"))
    if c == "original_language":
        s = s.where(s.isin(s.value_counts().head(8).index), "other")
    Xhgb[c] = s.astype("category")
OOF["Gradient boosting (sklearn)"] = cv_predict(
    HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=15, min_samples_leaf=40, l2_regularization=1.0,
                                   categorical_features="from_dtype", random_state=560), Xhgb)

cmp = pd.DataFrame([summary_row("Baseline (b)", oof_b, False)] + [summary_row(k, v) for k, v in OOF.items()]).set_index("model")
display(cmp.sort_values("AUC", ascending=False))
'''),
md(r'''
### 4d. Statistical fit of each feature (logistic regression, all training films)

- **McFadden pseudo-R²:** 1 − (log-likelihood of the model ÷ that of a model with no features). 0.2–0.4 is a good fit for logistic regression.
- **AIC:** fit penalized for the number of parameters; lower is better. A feature earns its place if removing it **raises** AIC by more than about 2.
- **Likelihood-ratio test:** refit without the feature (all its categories at once); p < 0.05 = keep.

Budget enters as log budget and its square (its curve). Numbers are standardized; categories are compared with PG-13 / Drama / US only / Major / Friday / Original / English.
'''),
code(r'''
REF = {"mpaa_rating": "PG-13", "primary_genre": "Drama", "origin_group": "US only", "distributor_group": "Major", "release_weekday": "Friday",
       "source_group": "Original", "original_language": "en"}
LABEL = {"mpaa_rating": "MPAA rating", "primary_genre": "primary genre", "origin_group": "origin (US / non-US)", "distributor_group": "distributor group",
         "release_weekday": "release weekday", "source_group": "source group", "original_language": "original language"}
NUM_GROUPS = {"budget (log + curve)": ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"], "runtime": ["runtime_min"], "release month": ["release_month"],
              "sequel": ["sequel"], "major producer": ["major_producer"],
              "director track record": ["director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history"],
              "writer track record": ["writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history"],
              "company track record": ["company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history"],
              "rating-overlap competition": ["rating_overlap_competition"]}


def design(X, nums, cats):
    """statsmodels design matrix: standardized numbers (median-filled), budget curve, dummies vs reference."""
    S = X.copy()
    S["log_budget_c"] = S["log_budget"] - S["log_budget"].mean()
    S["log_budget_sq"] = S["log_budget_c"] ** 2
    terms = ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"] + nums
    for c in terms:
        v = S[c].astype(float).fillna(S[c].astype(float).median())
        S[c] = (v - v.mean()) / v.std()
    dums = []
    for c in cats:
        dm = pd.get_dummies(S[c], prefix=c, dtype=float)
        dums.append(dm.drop(columns=f"{c}_{REF[c]}" if f"{c}_{REF[c]}" in dm else dm.columns[0]))
    XS = sm.add_constant(pd.concat([S[terms]] + dums, axis=1))
    groups = {g: cols for g, cols in NUM_GROUPS.items() if all(c in XS for c in cols)}
    groups.update({LABEL[c]: [x for x in XS.columns if x.startswith(c + "_")] for c in cats})
    return XS, groups


def logit(XS, cols):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        return sm.Logit(yl, XS[cols]).fit(disp=0, maxiter=500, method="newton")


def fit_table(XS, groups):
    full = logit(XS, list(XS.columns))
    rows = []
    for g, cols in groups.items():
        red = logit(XS, [c for c in XS.columns if c not in cols]); lr = 2 * (full.llf - red.llf)
        rows.append({"feature": g, "terms": len(cols), "LR chi2": round(lr, 1), "p": chi2.sf(lr, len(cols)), "AIC if removed (+ = worse)": round(red.aic - full.aic, 1)})
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("feature").sort_values("LR chi2", ascending=False)
    t["verdict"] = np.where((t["p"] < 0.05) & (t["AIC if removed (+ = worse)"] > 2), "keep", np.where(t["p"] < 0.10, "borderline", "drop candidate"))
    t["p-value"] = t.pop("p").map(lambda p: f"{p:.1e}" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")
    return full, t


XS, G = design(D, NUMS, CATS)
null_ll = sm.Logit(yl, XS[["const"]]).fit(disp=0).llf
full, ft = fit_table(XS, G)
print(f"All candidate features: {len(XS.columns) - 1} terms; McFadden pseudo-R2 {1 - full.llf / null_ll:.3f}; AIC {full.aic:.1f}")
display(ft)
'''),
md(r'''
### 4e. Blank categories leak the outcome too

A "(blank)" source or origin marks a film the databases barely documented; in the training years every such film is a loser (perfect separation in 4d). That is the same leak as the `_missing` flags, hiding inside the categories. **Fix:** merge each blank into the most common category (distributor "Blank" → "Other") so the model can't use "undocumented" as a signal.
'''),
code(r'''
Xclean = Xall.copy()
for c in CATS:
    Xclean[c] = Xclean[c].replace("(blank)", Xclean.loc[Xclean[c] != "(blank)", c].mode()[0])
Xclean["distributor_group"] = Xclean["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
res = []
for name in ["Logistic regression", "XGBoost", "Random forest"]:
    o = cv_predict(MODELS[name], Xclean); cap, prec = capture_at(o, yl)
    res.append({"model": name, "AUC with blank categories": round(roc_auc_score(yl, OOF[name]), 3), "AUC blanks merged": round(roc_auc_score(yl, o), 3),
                "recall @20% (merged)": f"{cap:.1%}", "precision @20% (merged)": f"{prec:.1%}"})
display(pd.DataFrame(res).set_index("model"))
print("Training films with any blank category:", int(((Xall[CATS] == "(blank)").any(axis=1) | (Xall["distributor_group"] == "Blank")).sum()))
'''),
md(r'''
### 4f. Final model

Agreed feature set (Tanner, 2026-11-27, `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §20):
- **Dropped:** release month, writer track record, original language (each failed the likelihood-ratio test in 4d and *lowered* AIC when removed); source group (failed once blanks were merged: p = 0.39, AIC −4.8 when removed; genre, rating and sequel cover it).
- **Kept as borderline:** director track record, major producer.
- **Blanks merged** as in 4e. **Main model:** logistic regression. **Challenger:** XGBoost, same features.
'''),
code(r'''
NUMS_F = ["runtime_min", "sequel", "major_producer", "director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history",
          "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history", "rating_overlap_competition"]
CATS_F = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday"]
XF = D[["log_budget"] + NUMS_F + CATS_F].copy()
MODE_F = {c: XF.loc[XF[c] != "(blank)", c].mode()[0] for c in CATS_F}             # training modes, reused for the test set

**Measures**
- **Recall @20%** (winners caught) = share of all winners that land in the top 20% picks. With 33% winners, random picks catch 20%; the best possible is 60%.
- **Precision @20%** (hit rate) = share of the picks that are winners (random: 33%).
- **AUC** = ranking quality over all films (0.5 = random, 1 = perfect).

**Ties:** picks use a stable sort (`kind="stable"`), so films with equal scores are always broken in the same order on every machine. def top_k(score, k=0.2):
    """Indices of the top k share of films by score; stable sort so ties break the same way everywhere."""
    return np.argsort(-score, kind="stable")[:int(round(k * len(score)))]


def capture_at(score, y, k=0.2):

def summary_row(name, s, with_logloss=True):

REF = {"mpaa_rating": "PG-13", "primary_genre": "Drama", "origin_group": "US only", "distributor_group": "Major", "release_weekday": "Friday",
       "source_group": "Original", "original_language": "en"}
LABEL = {"mpaa_rating": "MPAA rating", "primary_genre": "primary genre", "origin_group": "origin (US / non-US)", "distributor_group": "distributor group",
         "release_weekday": "release weekday", "source_group": "source group", "original_language": "original language"}
NUM_GROUPS = {"budget (log + curve)": ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"], "runtime": ["runtime_min"], "release month": ["release_month"],
              "sequel": ["sequel"], "major producer": ["major_producer"],
              "director track record": ["director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history"],
              "writer track record": ["writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history"],
              "company track record": ["company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history"],
              "rating-overlap competition": ["rating_overlap_competition"]}


def design(X, nums, cats):
    """statsmodels design matrix: standardized numbers (median-filled), budget curve, dummies vs reference."""
    S = X.copy()
    S["log_budget_c"] = S["log_budget"] - S["log_budget"].mean()
    S["log_budget_sq"] = S["log_budget_c"] ** 2
    terms = ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"] + nums
    for c in terms:
        v = S[c].astype(float).fillna(S[c].astype(float).median())
        S[c] = (v - v.mean()) / v.std()
    dums = []
    for c in cats:
        dm = pd.get_dummies(S[c], prefix=c, dtype=float)
        dums.append(dm.drop(columns=f"{c}_{REF[c]}" if f"{c}_{REF[c]}" in dm else dm.columns[0]))
    XS = sm.add_constant(pd.concat([S[terms]] + dums, axis=1))
    groups = {g: cols for g, cols in NUM_GROUPS.items() if all(c in XS for c in cols)}
    groups.update({LABEL[c]: [x for x in XS.columns if x.startswith(c + "_")] for c in cats})
    return XS, groups

display(cmp.sort_values("AUC", ascending=False))
'''),
md(r'''
### 4d. Statistical fit of each feature (logistic regression, all training films)

- **McFadden pseudo-R²:** 1 − (log-likelihood of the model ÷ that of a model with no features). 0.2–0.4 is a good fit for logistic regression.
- **AIC:** fit penalized for the number of parameters; lower is better. A feature earns its place if removing it **raises** AIC by more than about 2.
- **Likelihood-ratio test:** refit without the feature (all its categories at once); p < 0.05 = keep.

Budget enters as log budget and its square (its curve). Numbers are standardized; categories are compared with PG-13 / Drama / US only / Major / Friday / Original / English.
'''),
code(r'''
REF = {"mpaa_rating": "PG-13", "primary_genre": "Drama", "origin_group": "US only", "distributor_group": "Major", "release_weekday": "Friday",
       "source_group": "Original", "original_language": "en"}
LABEL = {"mpaa_rating": "MPAA rating", "primary_genre": "primary genre", "origin_group": "origin (US / non-US)", "distributor_group": "distributor group",
         "release_weekday": "release weekday", "source_group": "source group", "original_language": "original language"}
NUM_GROUPS = {"budget (log + curve)": ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"], "runtime": ["runtime_min"], "release month": ["release_month"],
              "sequel": ["sequel"], "major producer": ["major_producer"],
              "director track record": ["director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history"],
              "writer track record": ["writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history"],
              "company track record": ["company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history"],
              "rating-overlap competition": ["rating_overlap_competition"]}


def design(X, nums, cats):
    """statsmodels design matrix: standardized numbers (median-filled), budget curve, dummies vs reference."""
    S = X.copy()
    S["log_budget_c"] = S["log_budget"] - S["log_budget"].mean()
    S["log_budget_sq"] = S["log_budget_c"] ** 2
    terms = ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"] + nums
    for c in terms:
        v = S[c].astype(float).fillna(S[c].astype(float).median())
        S[c] = (v - v.mean()) / v.std()
    dums = []
    for c in cats:
        dm = pd.get_dummies(S[c], prefix=c, dtype=float)
        dums.append(dm.drop(columns=f"{c}_{REF[c]}" if f"{c}_{REF[c]}" in dm else dm.columns[0]))
    XS = sm.add_constant(pd.concat([S[terms]] + dums, axis=1))
    groups = {g: cols for g, cols in NUM_GROUPS.items() if all(c in XS for c in cols)}
    groups.update({LABEL[c]: [x for x in XS.columns if x.startswith(c + "_")] for c in cats})
    return XS, groups


def logit(XS, cols):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        return sm.Logit(yl, XS[cols]).fit(disp=0, maxiter=500, method="newton")


def fit_table(XS, groups):
    full = logit(XS, list(XS.columns))
    rows = []
    for g, cols in groups.items():
        red = logit(XS, [c for c in XS.columns if c not in cols]); lr = 2 * (full.llf - red.llf)
        rows.append({"feature": g, "terms": len(cols), "LR chi2": round(lr, 1), "p": chi2.sf(lr, len(cols)), "AIC if removed (+ = worse)": round(red.aic - full.aic, 1)})
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("feature").sort_values("LR chi2", ascending=False)
    t["verdict"] = np.where((t["p"] < 0.05) & (t["AIC if removed (+ = worse)"] > 2), "keep", np.where(t["p"] < 0.10, "borderline", "drop candidate"))
    t["p-value"] = t.pop("p").map(lambda p: f"{p:.1e}" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")
    return full, t


XS, G = design(D, NUMS, CATS)
null_ll = sm.Logit(yl, XS[["const"]]).fit(disp=0).llf
full, ft = fit_table(XS, G)
print(f"All candidate features: {len(XS.columns) - 1} terms; McFadden pseudo-R2 {1 - full.llf / null_ll:.3f}; AIC {full.aic:.1f}")
display(ft)
'''),
md(r'''
### 4e. Blank categories leak the outcome too

A "(blank)" source or origin marks a film the databases barely documented; in the training years every such film is a loser (perfect separation in 4d). That is the same leak as the `_missing` flags, hiding inside the categories. **Fix:** merge each blank into the most common category (distributor "Blank" → "Other") so the model can't use "undocumented" as a signal.
'''),
code(r'''

Xclean["distributor_group"] = Xclean["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
res = []
for name in ["Logistic regression", "XGBoost", "Random forest"]:

    res.append({"model": name, "AUC with blank categories": round(roc_auc_score(yl, OOF[name]), 3), "AUC blanks merged": round(roc_auc_score(yl, o), 3),
                "recall @20% (merged)": f"{cap:.1%}", "precision @20% (merged)": f"{prec:.1%}"})
display(pd.DataFrame(res).set_index("model"))
print("Training films with any blank category:", int(((Xall[CATS] == "(blank)").any(axis=1) | (Xall["distributor_group"] == "Blank")).sum()))
'''),

Agreed feature set (Tanner, 2026-11-27, `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §20):
- **Dropped:** release month, writer track record, original language (each failed the likelihood-ratio test in 4d and *lowered* AIC when removed); source group (failed once blanks were merged: p = 0.39, AIC −4.8 when removed; genre, rating and sequel cover it).
- **Kept as borderline:** director track record, major producer.
- **Blanks merged** as in 4e. **Main model:** logistic regression. **Challenger:** XGBoost, same features.
'''),
code(r'''
NUMS_F = ["runtime_min", "sequel", "major_producer", "director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history",
          "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history", "rating_overlap_competition"]
CATS_F = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday"]
XF = D[["log_budget"] + NUMS_F + CATS_F].copy()
MODE_F = {c: XF.loc[XF[c] != "(blank)", c].mode()[0] for c in CATS_F}             # training modes, reused for the test set
for c in CATS_F:

XF["distributor_group"] = XF["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")

pre_lin_f = ColumnTransformer([

    ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMS_F),

pre_tree_f = ColumnTransformer([("num", "passthrough", ["log_budget"] + NUMS_F),

'''),

display(ft_f)
odds = pd.DataFrame({"odds ratio": np.exp(full_f.params), "95% low": np.exp(full_f.conf_int()[0]), "95% high": np.exp(full_f.conf_int()[1]),

md(r'''
## 5. Evaluation

Promoted from `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §21 (Tanner, run once on 2026-11-27).

### 5a. Test set 2016–2019 (pre-committed, single test)

Everything is frozen before this runs:
- **Model:** the §4f logistic regression, trained on **all** 2000–2015 films. Challenger: XGBoost, same features.
- **Baseline (b):** genre × budget-tier winner rate from 2000–2015 (smoothed as in §4b).
- **Selection:** the contract picks 20% **each year**, so the main result picks the top 20% within each release year. Pooled top 20% shown as a check.
- **Measures (A9):** recall (share of all test winners in the picks), precision (share of picks that are winners), AUC.
- **Evidence bar (A9):** beat the baseline by **≥ 5 points in recall**, with a **bootstrap 95% CI** (2,000 resamples of test films) that excludes 0.
- Nothing below changes the model. Any change after this point would be tuned on the test set and must be reported that way.
'''),
code(r'''
TEST = films[films["in_population"] & films["year"].between(2016, 2019)].reset_index(drop=True)
yt = TEST["winner"].astype(int).values
years = TEST["year"].astype(int).values
print(f"Test films: {len(TEST):,} (2016-19); winners {yt.mean():.1%}; by year: {TEST.groupby(years).size().to_dict()}")

keep_genres = set(TRN["primary_genre"].value_counts().loc[lambda s: s >= 40].index)


def prep(df):
    """Same transformations as the training data, with every choice learned from the training set."""
    d = df.copy()
    d["mpaa_rating"] = d["mpaa_rating"].replace({"NC-17": "R"})
    d["primary_genre"] = d["primary_genre"].where(d["primary_genre"].isin(keep_genres), "Other")
    for c in ["director", "company"]:
        d[f"{c}_has_history"] = d[f"{c}_prior_hit_rate"].notna().astype(int)
    for c in CATS_F:

    d["distributor_group"] = d["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
    return d[["log_budget"] + NUMS_F + CATS_F]


Xtest = prep(TEST)
p_logit = FINAL["Logistic regression (final)"].fit(XF, yl).predict_proba(Xtest)[:, 1]
p_xgb = FINAL["XGBoost (challenger)"].fit(XF, yl).predict_proba(Xtest)[:, 1]

p_base = g_te.map((rates["sum"] + 20 * yl.mean()) / (rates["size"] + 20)).fillna(yl.mean()).values
SCORES_T = {"Baseline (b)": p_base, "Logistic regression (final)": p_logit, "XGBoost (challenger)": p_xgb}


def pick_mask(score, yrs, k=0.2, per_year=True):
    mask = np.zeros(len(score), bool)
    for g in ([np.where(yrs == y)[0] for y in np.unique(yrs)] if per_year else [np.arange(len(score))]):
        mask[g[top_k(score[g], k)]] = True

def measures(score, y, yrs, per_year=True):

md(r'''
**What §4 shows** (run 2026-11-28, cross-validated inside 2000–15; matches `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §18–20 except where noted)

| Model (5-fold CV, 3,708 training films) | AUC (95% range) | Recall @20% | Precision @20% |
|---|---|---|---|
| Random 20% | 0.500 | 20% | 33% |
| Baseline (b): genre × budget tier | 0.609 (0.591–0.625) | 28.4% | 47.0% |
| Five model types, candidate features (4c) | 0.705–0.766 | 34.2–38.3% | 56.6–63.3% |
| **Final logistic regression (4f)** | **0.769 (0.754–0.785)** | **38.9%** | **64.3%** |
| XGBoost challenger, same features | 0.759 (0.742–0.777) | 37.3% | 61.7% |

- **Model choice:** logistic regression, XGBoost, scikit-learn gradient boosting and random forest are statistically tied (their AUC ranges overlap); the single tree is weaker. Logistic regression is the main model because it is at least as accurate, its probabilities are the best calibrated (lowest log loss, 0.526), and every effect can be stated as odds and tested.
- **Fit:** McFadden pseudo-R² 0.192, AIC 3,880. **All 12 features pass the likelihood-ratio test** (p ≤ 0.008) and raise AIC when removed.
- **Biggest effects (odds of a winner):** Horror 2.6×, Documentary 2.5×, G rating 2.2×, Animation 1.9×, Comedy 1.6× vs Drama/PG-13; Wednesday release 1.5× vs Friday; sequel 1.34× and company hit rate 1.33× per SD; more same/neighboring-rating competition 0.78× per SD; R 0.58×, non-US 0.43×, Specialty 0.32× and Other distributors 0.27×, NR 0.06×.
- **Budget is negative once the rest is known (0.44× per SD):** among films with the same distributor, rating and genre, cheaper films more often clear 1.25×. Big budgets look good alone only because they come with majors and sequels.
- **Blanks:** merging blank categories costs almost nothing (logistic 0.766 → 0.764), so the model wasn't leaning on them, but it can no longer use "undocumented film" as a signal.
- **Difference from Tanner's run:** the baseline's recall is 28.4% here vs 28.0% (stable tie-breaking, see §4 intro). Model results are identical.
'''),

content.content:
## What this PR does
- **Test set 2016–19, evaluated once** (`Edwards-A10.ipynb` §21). The final logistic regression (12 features, trained on 2000–15) picked the top 20% of films each year.

  | | AUC | Winners caught | Picks that won |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline | 0.621 | 31.9% | 57% |
  | Model | **0.831** | **45.1%** | **80%** |

  That's +13.2 points of winners caught (bootstrap 95% CI +7.8 to +17.6), so **the evidence standard is met**. The probabilities are well calibrated, and every test year beats the baseline.
- **Amendment A9 is in the contract:** the decision is now picking the 20% most likely winners. The pipeline writes a `winner` column as *the* label; `loser` is kept only so early exploration still runs.
- **Winner framing everywhere:** the master notebook (retitled *Picking Winners Among US Theatrical Films*), README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, FEATURE_IDEAS and PLAN.md.
- **Setup after pulling:** reinstall `requirements.txt` (it adds statsmodels and xgboost), then rerun `01_clean_dataset.ipynb` to get the `winner` column.

## Handoff to Matt: what's next
Tanner is pausing here. The remaining work maps mostly onto CRISP-DM **Phase 5, Evaluation**, with the write-up falling in **Phase 6, Deployment**. Your plan's phase numbers line up with CRISP-DM's from Phase 1 through Phase 6.

| What's next | CRISP-DM phase and step |
|---|---|
| Test vs. baseline (S1), precision, calibration, stress test | **5. Evaluation, step 1:** test results against the Phase 1 success criteria, which your contract states as the evidence standard |
| Sensitivity checks, ablation | **5. Evaluation, step 1**, as checks that the result holds. They overlap with Modeling's technical checks. |
| Error analysis, responsible use, prohibited uses | **5. Evaluation, step 3:** review the process for bias, privacy and harm |
| Value (break-even) | **5. Evaluation, step 1:** translate performance into business impact and compare it to cost |
| Decision policy (20% capacity, human review) | **5. Evaluation, step 4:** deployment readiness |
| Verdict (continue / pilot / redirect / satisfice / stop) | **5. Evaluation, step 5:** deploy, iterate, reframe or cancel |
| Reopening evidence (marketing spend, etc.) | **5. Evaluation, step 5**, the "reframe" path. It loops back to Business Understanding. |
| Appendix D (independent rebuild) | **5. Evaluation, step 3:** audit whether the earlier phases were done thoroughly |
| Report, deck, traceability | **6. Deployment, step 3:** the final report and presentation |
| Pilot recommendation, monitoring and limitations | **6. Deployment, steps 2 and 5:** monitoring plan and feedback loops, written up as recommendations |
| Fresh Run All, final zip, `ai_logs`, AI disclosure | Course packaging. It sits outside CRISP-DM but supports Deployment's documentation step. |

**How the phases differ here**
- **Modeling** asks whether the model works technically. We finished that when we chose and locked the model.
- **Evaluation** asks whether it meets the business objectives set in Phase 1 and whether the organization should move forward. The contract's evidence standard is the success criteria from that earlier phase.
- **Deployment** is the report and deck, since our deliverables are documents instead of a live system.

Evaluation step 6, formal stakeholder sign-off, has no real counterpart here. Our owner is a stand-in role, so the report should say so.

**Already done for step 1:** the 2016–19 test vs the baseline, precision, and calibration (§21). **Still open in step 1:**
- the 2020–23 COVID stress test (A5)
- sensitivity at 1× and 1.5× and the $100K floor (A2)
- ablation

## Note for Matt's AI
1. **If Matt approves this work, move it into `notebooks/A10-master.ipynb`** with a PR, following the README rule that the master only gets finished, verified work. Never edit `Edwards-A10.ipynb`, since it's Tanner's personal notebook.
   - The master already has §1–3 (Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation). It has §4–5 as text only.
   - It still needs the **code** from `Edwards-A10.ipynb` §18–21: the baseline, model comparison, fit tests (pseudo-R², AIC, likelihood-ratio tests), the final model, and the one-time test evaluation.
   - All of it must re-run from `data/clean/films_clean.csv`.
2. **Don't retune anything on 2016–19.** That test has been used. Any change to the model now has to be reported as tuned on the test.
3. **Present results as winners** (`winner` column, picking the top 20%), never losers. This is amendment A9.
4. **Open items:**
   - Matt's A8 draft is still pending in `A10_contract_amendments_PROPOSED.md`. A9 and A7 cover its question and label, so close it or reconcile it.
   - The title matcher misses a few big films (*F9*, *The Butler*).
   - `audience_score` should prefer Rotten Tomatoes' score over TMDB's.
   - The AI log (row 7) is still PARTIAL. Its finalize command is in `PLAN.md`; re-apply the escape-safe email redaction afterward.
5. **The team summary page** (charts, features, model results) is "A10 EDA Findings". Tanner can share the link.

The 2020–23 data looks like this:

| Year | Films | Winner rate | Median return |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2016–19 (test) | 183–256 per year | 31–43% | 0.63–0.87× |
| 2020 | 67 | 16% | 0.33× |
| 2021 | 99 | 18% | 0.54× |
| 2022 | 105 | 32% | 0.67× |
| 2023 | 99 | 35% | 0.77× |

That's 370 stress-test films. In 2020–21, winners fall to about half the usual rate, then they recover in 2022–23.

**Proposed design for the stress test** (amendment A5 says to report it separately from the main test; it isn't a pass/fail test):

1. **Main result: the frozen model, unchanged.** It's trained on 2000–15 and picks the top 20% each year, as in §5a. Same measures as §5a: recall, precision and AUC vs the baseline, with a bootstrap CI. I'd report each year and two periods, **2020–21** (theater closures) and **2022–23** (recovery).
2. **Calibration check.** The model has never seen a COVID year, so it will likely predict roughly a 35% winner rate when the actual rate is about 17%. The useful question is whether it still *ranks* films well even when its probabilities are off. For a "top 20% each year" decision, ranking is what matters, and the report should say that plainly.
3. **Secondary result (optional): the same model refit on 2000–19** with identical settings and no tuning, then applied to 2020–23. This is what a studio would actually run in 2020. It would be clearly labeled as a variant, not the pre-committed result.
4. **Caveats written alongside:** small samples (2020 has only 13 picks), and 2020–21 films that streamed the same day they opened in theaters, whose US box office understates them. Our label counts theaters only.

**Where:** a new standalone section at the end of `Sorensen-A10.ipynb`. It reads only `films_clean.csv` and rebuilds the frozen model there, so it doesn't rerun your old §2–4. If you approve the results, it moves into the master §5b by PR, the same way as today.

Should I go ahead, and should the secondary refit on 2000–19 (point 3) be included?
yes, yes
I'll build the stress-test section in your notebook. It starts with a sanity check that the rebuilt model reproduces the 2016–19 test result exactly, and only then scores 2020–23.

from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, SplineTransformer, StandardScaler

FC = pd.read_csv(Path("../data/clean") / "films_clean.csv", low_memory=False)
POP = FC[FC["in_population"]].reset_index(drop=True)
POP["year"] = POP["year"].astype(int)

          "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history", "rating_overlap_competition"]
CATS_F = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday"]
TIERS = ([0, 5e6, 20e6, 60e6, np.inf], ["$1-5M", "$5-20M", "$20-60M", "$60M+"])


def fit_final(train):
    """Master §4f model and baseline (b), with every data choice learned from `train`. Returns score(df) -> (model, baseline)."""
    y = train["winner"].astype(int).values
    keep_genres = set(train["primary_genre"].value_counts().loc[lambda s: s >= 40].index)

    def base_prep(df):
        d = df.copy()
        d["mpaa_rating"] = d["mpaa_rating"].replace({"NC-17": "R"})
        d["primary_genre"] = d["primary_genre"].where(d["primary_genre"].isin(keep_genres), "Other")
        for c in ["director", "company"]:
            d[f"{c}_has_history"] = d[f"{c}_prior_hit_rate"].notna().astype(int)
        for c in CATS_F:

        for c in CATS_F:
            d[c] = d[c].replace("(blank)", modes[c])
        d["distributor_group"] = d["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
        return d[["log_budget"] + NUMS_F + CATS_F]

    pre = ColumnTransformer([
        ("budget", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3)), ["log_budget"]),
        ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMS_F),
        ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20), CATS_F)])
    model = make_pipeline(pre, LogisticRegression(max_iter=3000, C=0.5)).fit(prep(train), y)

    for y in np.unique(yrs):

    return mask

    w = pick_mask(score, yrs)
    return {"recall": y[w].sum() / y.sum(), "precision": y[w].mean(), "AUC": roc_auc_score(y, score)}

    for name, (a, z) in periods.items():

        sm_, sb = score_fn(P)
        y, yrs = P["winner"].astype(int).values, P["year"].values
        m, b = measures(sm_, y, yrs), measures(sb, y, yrs)
        rows.append({"period": name, "films": len(P), "picks": int(pick_mask(sm_, yrs).sum()), "winner rate": f"{y.mean():.0%}",
                     "model: mean predicted chance": f"{sm_.mean():.0%}",
                     "baseline recall": f"{b['recall']:.1%}", "model recall": f"{m['recall']:.1%}", "best possible recall": f"{min(1, .2 / y.mean()):.0%}",
                     "baseline precision": f"{b['precision']:.1%}", "model precision": f"{m['precision']:.1%}",
                     "baseline AUC": round(b["AUC"], 3), "model AUC": round(m["AUC"], 3)})
        store[name] = (P, sm_, sb, y, yrs)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("period"), store


tab_frozen, S_frozen = period_table(score_frozen)
display(tab_frozen.T)

def gain_ci(store, names, B=2000, seed=2020):
    """Model minus baseline recall (points) and AUC, bootstrap 95% CI over films; picks re-made per year in every resample."""
    out = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

"""Append (or replace) the standalone stress-test section at the end of Sorensen-A10.ipynb."""
import json
import sys
import uuid

path, findings_path = sys.argv[1], (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)
MARK = "## 5. Stress test 2020–2023"
nb = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))
cells = [c for c in nb["cells"] if not c.get("metadata", {}).get("stress_section")]


def cell(kind, s):
    c = {"cell_type": kind, "id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "metadata": {"stress_section": True}, "source": s.strip("\n").splitlines(True)}
    if kind == "code":
        c.update(execution_count=None, outputs=[])
    return c


md = lambda s: cell("markdown", s)
code = lambda s: cell("code", s)

NEW = [
md(MARK + r''' (Matt, 2026-11-28)

**Plan step 21, contract amendment A5:** the COVID-era years are reported **separately** from the 2016–19 test. They are a stress test, not a pass/fail check.

**Standalone section:** it reads only `data/clean/films_clean.csv` and rebuilds the final model from `A10-master.ipynb` §4f (12 features, logistic regression), so the earlier sections of this notebook don't need to run.

**Design (agreed with Matt, 2026-11-28)**
1. **Main result: the frozen model,** trained on 2000–2015 and unchanged, picks the top 20% of films each year (as in master §5a). Results by year and for two periods: **2020–21** (theater closures, films streaming the same day they open) and **2022–23** (recovery).
2. **Calibration:** the model has never seen a COVID year, so its chances are expected to run high. The question is whether it still **ranks** films well, which is all the top-20%-each-year decision needs.
3. **Secondary result: the same model refit on 2000–2019** (same settings, nothing tuned), as a studio would actually have run it in 2020. Labeled as a variant.

**Caveats:** small samples (2020 has 67 films, so 13 picks); the label counts US **theatrical** box office only, so films that went to streaming the same day they opened look weaker than they were.
'''),
code(r'''
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, SplineTransformer, StandardScaler

FC = pd.read_csv(Path("../data/clean") / "films_clean.csv", low_memory=False)
POP = FC[FC["in_population"]].reset_index(drop=True)
POP["year"] = POP["year"].astype(int)
NUMS_F = ["runtime_min", "sequel", "major_producer", "director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history",
          "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history", "rating_overlap_competition"]
CATS_F = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday"]
TIERS = ([0, 5e6, 20e6, 60e6, np.inf], ["$1-5M", "$5-20M", "$20-60M", "$60M+"])


def fit_final(train):
    """Master §4f model and baseline (b), with every data choice learned from `train`. Returns score(df) -> (model, baseline)."""
    y = train["winner"].astype(int).values
    keep_genres = set(train["primary_genre"].value_counts().loc[lambda s: s >= 40].index)

    def base_prep(df):
        d = df.copy()
        d["mpaa_rating"] = d["mpaa_rating"].replace({"NC-17": "R"})
        d["primary_genre"] = d["primary_genre"].where(d["primary_genre"].isin(keep_genres), "Other")
        for c in ["director", "company"]:
            d[f"{c}_has_history"] = d[f"{c}_prior_hit_rate"].notna().astype(int)
        for c in CATS_F:
            d[c] = d[c].astype(object).fillna("(blank)").astype(str)
        return d

    dt = base_prep(train)
    modes = {c: dt.loc[dt[c] != "(blank)", c].mode()[0] for c in CATS_F}

    def prep(df):
        d = base_prep(df)
        for c in CATS_F:
            d[c] = d[c].replace("(blank)", modes[c])
        d["distributor_group"] = d["distributor_group"].replace("Blank", "Other")
        return d[["log_budget"] + NUMS_F + CATS_F]

    pre = ColumnTransformer([
        ("budget", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3)), ["log_budget"]),
        ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMS_F),
        ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20), CATS_F)])
    model = make_pipeline(pre, LogisticRegression(max_iter=3000, C=0.5)).fit(prep(train), y)
    group = lambda df: df["primary_genre"].fillna("(blank)") + " | " + pd.cut(df["fin_budget"], *TIERS).astype(str)
    r = pd.Series(y).groupby(group(train).values).agg(["sum", "size"])
    smooth = (r["sum"] + 20 * y.mean()) / (r["size"] + 20)
    return lambda df: (model.predict_proba(prep(df))[:, 1], group(df).map(smooth).fillna(y.mean()).values)


def top_k(score, k=0.2):
    return np.argsort(-score, kind="stable")[:int(round(k * len(score)))]


def pick_mask(score, yrs, k=0.2):
    mask = np.zeros(len(score), bool)
    for y in np.unique(yrs):
        g = np.where(yrs == y)[0]
        mask[g[top_k(score[g], k)]] = True
    return mask


def measures(score, y, yrs):
    w = pick_mask(score, yrs)
    return {"recall": y[w].sum() / y.sum(), "precision": y[w].mean(), "AUC": roc_auc_score(y, score)}


score_frozen = fit_final(POP[POP["year"].le(2015)])

# Sanity check: must reproduce master §5a exactly (AUC 0.831, recall 45.1%, precision 80.1%; baseline 32.2% / 57.3%)
T = POP[POP["year"].between(2016, 2019)].reset_index(drop=True)
pm, pb = score_frozen(T)
yt, yrs_t = T["winner"].astype(int).values, T["year"].values
m, b = measures(pm, yt, yrs_t), measures(pb, yt, yrs_t)
print(f"Check vs master §5a, 2016-19: model AUC {m['AUC']:.3f}, recall {m['recall']:.1%}, precision {m['precision']:.1%}; "
      f"baseline recall {b['recall']:.1%}, precision {b['precision']:.1%}")
assert round(m["AUC"], 3) == 0.831 and round(100 * m["recall"], 1) == 45.1, "rebuilt model does not match master §5a"
'''),
md(r'''
### 5a. Frozen model (trained 2000–2015) on the stress years
'''),
code(r'''
PERIODS = {"2016-19 (test, for reference)": (2016, 2019), "2020-21 (closures)": (2020, 2021), "2022-23 (recovery)": (2022, 2023),
           "2020-23 (all stress years)": (2020, 2023)}


def period_table(score_fn, periods=PERIODS):
    rows, store = [], {}
    for name, (a, z) in periods.items():
        P = POP[POP["year"].between(a, z)].reset_index(drop=True)
        sm_, sb = score_fn(P)
        y, yrs = P["winner"].astype(int).values, P["year"].values
        m, b = measures(sm_, y, yrs), measures(sb, y, yrs)
        rows.append({"period": name, "films": len(P), "picks": int(pick_mask(sm_, yrs).sum()), "winner rate": f"{y.mean():.0%}",
                     "model: mean predicted chance": f"{sm_.mean():.0%}",
                     "baseline recall": f"{b['recall']:.1%}", "model recall": f"{m['recall']:.1%}", "best possible recall": f"{min(1, .2 / y.mean()):.0%}",
                     "baseline precision": f"{b['precision']:.1%}", "model precision": f"{m['precision']:.1%}",
                     "baseline AUC": round(b["AUC"], 3), "model AUC": round(m["AUC"], 3)})
        store[name] = (P, sm_, sb, y, yrs)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("period"), store


tab_frozen, S_frozen = period_table(score_frozen)
display(tab_frozen.T)
'''),
code(r'''
def gain_ci(store, names, B=2000, seed=2020):
    """Model minus baseline recall (points) and AUC, bootstrap 95% CI over films; picks re-made per year in every resample."""
    out = []
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    for name in names:
        P, sm_, sb, y, yrs = store[name]
        d_rec, d_auc = [], []
        for _ in range(B):
            i = rng.integers(0, len(y), len(y))
            mm, bb = measures(sm_[i], y[i], yrs[i]), measures(sb[i], y[i], yrs[i])
            d_rec.append(100 * (mm["recall"] - bb["recall"])); d_auc.append(mm["AUC"] - bb["AUC"])
        mm, bb = measures(sm_, y, yrs), measures(sb, y, yrs)
        out.append({"period": name, "recall gain (pts)": round(100 * (mm["recall"] - bb["recall"]), 1),
                    "95% CI": f"{np.percentile(d_rec, 2.5):+.1f} to {np.percentile(d_rec, 97.5):+.1f}",
                    "AUC gain": round(mm["AUC"] - bb["AUC"], 3), "AUC 95% CI": f"{np.percentile(d_auc, 2.5):+.3f} to {np.percentile(d_auc, 97.5):+.3f}"})
    return pd.DataFrame(out).set_index("period")


STRESS = ["2020-21 (closures)", "2022-23 (recovery)", "2020-23 (all stress years)"]
print("Frozen model vs baseline (b), top 20% each year:")
display(gain_ci(S_frozen, STRESS))
'''),
md(r'''
### 5b. Calibration: does the model know the market shrank?

Predicted chance vs actual winner rate. For the stress years, films are split into fifths of predicted chance within the whole 2020–23 set.
'''),
code(r'''
yr_rows = []
for yv in range(2016, 2024):
    P = POP[POP["year"].eq(yv)].reset_index(drop=True)
    sm_, sb = score_frozen(P)
    y = P["winner"].astype(int).values
    m, b = measures(sm_, y, P["year"].values), measures(sb, y, P["year"].values)
    yr_rows.append({"year": yv, "films": len(P), "winners": int(y.sum()), "actual winner rate": y.mean(), "mean predicted chance": sm_.mean(),
                    "baseline recall": b["recall"], "model recall": m["recall"], "baseline precision": b["precision"],
                    "model precision": m["precision"], "model AUC": m["AUC"]})
YR = pd.DataFrame(yr_rows).set_index("year")
display(YR.style.format({c: "{:.0%}" for c in YR.columns if c not in ["films", "winners", "model AUC"]} | {"model AUC": "{:.3f}"}))

P, sm_, sb, y, yrs = S_frozen["2020-23 (all stress years)"]
cal = pd.DataFrame({"p": sm_, "y": y}).groupby(pd.qcut(sm_, 5, labels=["lowest 20%", "2", "3", "4", "highest 20%"]), observed=True).agg(
    films=("y", "size"), predicted=("p", "mean"), actual=("y", "mean"))
print("Calibration, 2020-23 (frozen model):")
display(cal.round(2))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3.8))
ax[0].plot(YR.index, 100 * YR["actual winner rate"], "o-", label="actual winner rate")
ax[0].plot(YR.index, 100 * YR["mean predicted chance"], "s--", label="model's mean predicted chance")
ax[0].axvspan(2019.5, 2023.5, color="#1baf7a", alpha=.12); ax[0].set(title="Winner rate: predicted vs actual (%)", ylim=(0, 60)); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8)
ax[1].plot(YR.index, 100 * YR["model precision"], "o-", label="model: picks that won")
ax[1].plot(YR.index, 100 * YR["baseline precision"], "s--", label="baseline: picks that won")
ax[1].plot(YR.index, 100 * YR["actual winner rate"], ":", color="gray", label="random picks")
ax[1].axvspan(2019.5, 2023.5, color="#1baf7a", alpha=.12); ax[1].set(title="Top 20% each year: share of picks that won (%)", ylim=(0, 100)); ax[1].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
'''),
code(r'''
pick = pick_mask(sm_, yrs)
show = ["title", "year", "fin_budget", "us_multiple", "distributor_group", "mpaa_rating"]
print("2020-23 picks that won the most:")
display(P[pick].nlargest(8, "us_multiple")[show])
print("2020-23 costliest misses (picked, but under 1.25x):")
display(P[pick & (y == 0)].nlargest(8, "fin_budget")[show])
print("2020-23 biggest winners the model did NOT pick:")
display(P[~pick & (y == 1)].assign(chance=sm_[~pick & (y == 1)]).nlargest(8, "us_multiple")[show + ["chance"]])
'''),
md(r'''
### 5c. Secondary: same model refit on 2000–2019

What a studio would have run in 2020: identical specification and settings, trained on every film through 2019. Not tuned; reported as a variant next to the frozen result.
'''),
code(r'''
score_refit = fit_final(POP[POP["year"].le(2019)])
tab_refit, S_refit = period_table(score_refit, {k: v for k, v in PERIODS.items() if k in STRESS})
display(tab_refit.T)
print("Refit model vs baseline (b, also learned on 2000-19), top 20% each year:")
display(gain_ci(S_refit, STRESS))
'''),
]
if findings_path:
    NEW.append(md(open(findings_path, encoding="utf-8").read()))

nb["cells"] = cells + NEW
json.dump(nb, open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
